title: Safai Saathi shared constants
description: Every number and every string that must match on both sides of a boundary. The Dart apps, the TypeScript Functions and the admin panel all read this one file. A value that appears in two codebases and is not here is a bug waiting to happen. PRD-2 section 0.4: 'one config file per project, same names'.

x-groups.tracking: The location engine's cadence and thresholds.
x-groups.arrival: The arrival alert's geometry and freshness.
x-groups.identity: Claim names, formats and reason codes. A mismatch here is a security bug or a broken message.
x-groups.binding: The device-claim rate limit and the claim modes.

GPS_INTERVAL_SEC.note: The normal location write cadence. The arrival alert sees one write per this interval.

LOW_BATTERY_PCT.note: Below this, the slow cadence applies.

MIN_MOVE_M.note: The movement threshold below which a location write is skipped.

HEARTBEAT_SEC.note: The write policy's heartbeat. Forces a write even if the van has not moved.

ARRIVAL_ALERT_RADIUS_M.note: How close the van must be to the ward boundary before the citizen is alerted. PRD-2 section 0.6 says 500. The office asked for 100. The measured distance is from the ward BOUNDARY, not the centre, so the check is 'distance(centre) <= radiusM + ARRIVAL_ALERT_RADIUS_M'.

STALE_LOCATION_SEC.note: A location older than this is not trusted. The server uses it to decide whether to alert. The device uses it to decide whether to show 'last seen X min ago'.

OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_MIN.note: A van with no location write for this long is marked offline.

DUPLICATE_RADIUS_M.note: Two complaints closer than this are candidates for merging.

ESCALATION_L1_HOURS.note: An unresolved complaint escalates to level 1 after this.

ESCALATION_L2_HOURS.note: An unresolved complaint escalates to level 2 after this.

MISSED_REPORT_THRESHOLD.note: This many missed-collection reports in one ward today triggers the inspector alert.

MAX_COMPLAINTS_PER_DEVICE_PER_DAY.note: The rate limit per device per IST day.

DEPOT_DWELL_LIMIT_HOURS.note: Continuous dwell inside DEPOT_RADIUS_M that auto-ends the shift.

DEPOT_DWELL_RESET_M.note: Moving this far outside the depot restarts the dwell clock.

AVG_VAN_SPEED_KMPH.note: The fallback speed for the straight-line ETA estimate.

CLAIM_VAN_ID.note: The claim name for the van the session is bound to.

CLAIM_DRIVER_ID.note: The claim name for the driver's badge code. This is the phone-number wall.

CLAIM_DEVICE_ID.note: The claim name for the citizen's install id. Q6.

CLAIM_ROUTE_ID.note: The claim name for the route the citizen's ward belongs to.

CLAIM_CURRENT_TRIP_ID.note: The claim name for the open trip. Lets a rule be a pure token check.

CLAIM_STAFF_ID.note: The claim name for the staff member's doc id.

CLAIM_WARD_IDS.note: The claim name for the staff member's ward scope. The claim NAME is a string. The claim's VALUE is an array of ward ids. Every other CLAIM_ constant has a string value, so this one carries an explicit claimValueType.

CLAIM_ROLE.note: The claim name for the staff role.

PHONE_MASK_FORMAT.note: The exact masked phone shape. A different length breaks the confirm card's layout.

DRIVER_CODE_PATTERN.note: The driver doc id format. The callable rejects what the admin panel normalizes.

SHIFT_CONFLICT_VAN_HELD.note: Reason code: the van is on shift with another driver. Q2.

SHIFT_CONFLICT_ALREADY_CLAIMED.note: Reason code: another phone already holds the binding. Q1 and Q2.

SHIFT_CONFLICT_STALE_MARKER.note: Reason code: vans.currentTripId points at a trip of a different van. Q2.

VAN_DEVICE_CLAIM_MODE_FIRST.note: Q1. The binding was created by the first phone with a valid code.

VAN_DEVICE_CLAIM_MODE_PREPROVISIONED.note: Phase 11 hardening. The office had already written the binding.
